skills.name: Political, economic and social change in German Kamerun

note.text: German colonial rule created administrative institutions and expanded export-oriented production and transport. Plantations, roads and railways were connected to colonial economic aims; land and labour demands imposed serious costs. Mission and government activity brought forms of schooling and health provision but access was unequal and cultural change was contested. Calling a project development does not answer who controlled it, who benefited or who paid the costs. Assess different dimensions and communities rather than giving one unqualified verdict.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: German colonial rule created administrative institutions and expanded export-oriented production and transport. Plantations, roads and railways were connected to colonial economic aims; land and labour demands imposed serious costs. Mission and government activity brought forms of schooling and health provision but access was unequal and cultural change was contested. Calling a project development does not answer who controlled it, who benefited or who paid the costs. Assess different dimensions and communities rather than giving one unqualified verdict.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A railway can carry produce and people while also serving extraction and colonial control. A plantation can increase export output while taking land and demanding labour. A school record can show educational activity without proving universal access. The useful historical question is not merely whether a facility existed, but how it operated in an unequal colonial system.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: For each change, identify its purpose, beneficiaries and burdens. Separate infrastructure, political control and social institutions. Avoid using one building as proof that colonial rule was universally beneficial or using the existence of coercion to deny that any material change occurred.
